_why: Skips this repository's CI CANNOT arrange away, each named with the reason. Anything not listed here still fails the run. This file exists because a gate that cannot pass is indistinguishable from one that has not passed yet -- tests/test_prose_that_makes_a_claim.py opens with that sentence -- and without it every cell of the matrix is red forever for a reason nobody can fix. Adding an entry is a decision made in the open with a reason attached, which is exactly what scripts/ci_full_run_check.py's docstring asks for; deleting one is how you find out whether it is still true.
_measured: 2026-09-05, full serial run at e0dc8f9 in a clean clone, and again across six shards at 5046a3b. Four tests skipped; exactly one of them is structural.
_deliberately_absent: tests.test_uploads' three symlink tests skip on the operator's laptop because this Windows account holds no SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege. They are NOT listed: they run on Linux, and whether GitHub's Windows runner can create a symlink is unmeasured. If that cell goes red naming those three, that is the guard reporting something real and worth seeing once, not a defect in this file.

expected.tests.test_no_committed_identity::test_t: The wordlist it needs, _audit/_sanitisation_key.json, is the de-anonymisation key for the committed fixtures. It is gitignored ON PURPOSE (.gitignore:102) and must never reach a public runner, so it is absent from every clone and this test skips on every CI cell. Nothing about CI can change that, which is what makes it structural rather than an arrangement that stopped working. CORRECTED 2026-09-19: this entry used to say the test 'skips on every machine but the operator's', and that sentence was quietly false on his machine too. Git does not carry ignored files into a LINKED WORKTREE, so the key stayed in the main checkout and every worktree ran the shape half only -- which is where this entire agent fleet works. The path is now resolved through tests/repo_paths.py via git rev-parse --git-common-dir, the same repair the pre-commit hook took the same day for the same reason, so the test now RUNS in a worktree and still skips in a clone. If this entry is ever hit outside CI, check for a second path that is resolved against the worktree instead of the checkout.
expected.tests.test_a_verdict_earns_its_entry::te: The VERDICTS enrolment table ships EMPTY OF REAL ROWS ON PURPOSE, which that module's own docstring states and argues at length: enrolment ASSERTS a contract is safe, and the wave that built the certifier did not write any of the three candidate functions (_why_refused, _landing_class, is_read_url). Vouching for a function you did not write is the exact mistake the sibling shaper file exists to stop. So the table is empty and these four parametrise over it, giving pytest an empty parameter set. THE VACUITY IS COMPENSATED RATHER THAN IGNORED: each proof function is shown REJECTING over fixtures authored in that same file (test_the_proof_would_catch_*), none of which passes if its proof function is replaced by `return []`. CONDITIONAL, NOT PERMANENT -- the day anybody enrols a function they wrote, these four stop skipping and this entry should be deleted. Declared 2026-09-19 after CI named them; measured locally as 16 passed, 4 skipped, 'got empty parameter set for (claimant)'.

expected.tests.test_the_audience_reader_arrives_w: An ARMED TRIPWIRE for a reader that does not exist yet -- the test's own skip message says so: 'the reader does not exist yet, which is the state this file was written in; it arms itself'. It skips everywhere, including the build box, and it is not an arrangement that stopped working. CONDITIONAL: it fires the moment the audience reader lands without a contract test, which is the entire reason it was written early. Delete this entry then. Declared 2026-09-19.
expected.tests.test_uploads::test_a_windows_junct: A JUNCTION IS A WINDOWS-ONLY FILESYSTEM OBJECT, so this cannot run on the ubuntu cells and skips there; it RUNS on windows-latest, which is where the behaviour it guards actually exists. Note this is NOT one of the three symlink tests described in _deliberately_absent -- those skip on the operator's own Windows account for a privilege reason and are deliberately left undeclared. This one is a platform fact, measured on CI 2026-09-19: undeclared on both ubuntu cells, absent from the windows cell's list.
expected.tests.test_sweep_blobs_refuses_a_vacuous: THE SAME STRUCTURAL ABSENCE as the exact-value sweep entry above, one instrument along. This is the POSITIVE control for scripts/sweep_blobs_for_identity.py -- it sweeps a real commit range and asserts blobs were actually examined -- so it needs the same wordlist, _audit/_sanitisation_key.json, which is gitignored on purpose and must never reach a public runner. Absent from every clone, so this skips on every CI cell, forever, and nothing CI can arrange changes that. ONLY THE POSITIVE DIRECTION IS UNPROVEN HERE. The refusal cases in the same module -- garbage range, resolvable-but-empty range, the live caller shape -- all RUN on CI and need no key, because the range is validated before the wordlist is loaded. That ordering was the 2026-09-20 repair: beforehand load_wordlist() raised first and a garbage rev range was reported as a missing key on all three platforms. DECLARED 2026-09-20, after CI named it. The skip carries a sentence rather than a dot, so 'did not run' is said in the summary of every run instead of being indistinguishable from 'ran and found nothing'. Its author had written 'Never skipped' and argued a keyless environment should fail loudly; that was right for a developer box, where the absence is temporary and fixable, and wrong for CI, where it is permanent by design. A test that fails on every run forever teaches readers to scroll past red. If this entry is ever hit on a machine that HAS the key, do not widen it -- that is a path resolved against the wrong root, the same defect corrected in the entry above.
